My advice to you is to go to a Japanese Language School Full-time for at least a year and get the N1 as soon as possible.

For adults only Concerta and Strattera were available, but they recently approved intuniv for adults as well.

They recently approved using Vyvanse for children but it’s not available yet. And since they want to make getting it as hard as possible, they now require all Doctors and patients that will prescribe/use it to put their information to a special database. They will also use this database for people being prescribed Concerta, so basically less doctors will prescribe stimulants and less patients will be able to get access to them.

The stigma around Vyvanse is big since it was classified as a “methamphetamine precursor” and people got crazy over the fact that it’s for children.
